findings.title: The aligned conditioning identity overlaps proof text

frozen_source.claim: Proof step 2.1 puts a two-row aligned conditional-expectation identity between prose on the same source paragraph line.

rendered_evidence.visual_claim: The two-row expectation identity is rendered inline within proof step 2.1 and visibly collides with surrounding prose, making the passage difficult to read.

diagnostics.dom_evidence: The equation is emitted as a span.katex containing an mtable inside the step paragraph, not as a block .katex-display; the aligned array has two rows. This matches the inline overlap visible in the standalone tile.
diagnostics.reason: The item fits in one captured tile; DOM structure independently confirms inline multi-row math. This finding is overlap, not a horizontal-clipping claim.

findings.suggested_repair: Move the aligned identity into its own display-math paragraph, with explanatory prose before and after in separate paragraphs. Keep both conditional-expectation sides and the eventwise test unchanged.
repair_checks: Render the standalone ItemBody and confirm the two aligned rows occupy their own vertical block.
Confirm no prose intersects the equation at the captured width and at a narrower viewport.
Confirm both sides retain the same conditioning event and indicator.

findings.title: Three small CDF plots could distinguish the atom patterns

frozen_source.claim: Three explicit distribution functions contrast a purely atomic law, a continuous uniform law, and a mixed law.

findings.diagram_content: Use three aligned one-dimensional CDF plots on common axes: F_d is 0 before 0, 1/2 on [0,1), then 1; F_c is 0 before 0, rises linearly from 0 to 1 on [0,1], then stays 1; F_m jumps from 0 to 1/2 at 0, rises linearly to 1 on [0,1), then stays 1. Show open and closed endpoints at jumps and label jump sizes.
checks: Each plotted function is nondecreasing and right-continuous.
F_d has jumps 1/2 at 0 and 1; F_c has no jumps; F_m has one jump 1/2 at 0 and no jump at 1.
The axes and endpoint markers must not suggest a density for the purely atomic law.
findings.status_note: Optional teaching support, not a defect; the source already gives formulas and verifies the atom classification.

findings.title: A directed three-cycle could make the periodic counterexample immediate

frozen_source.claim: The deterministic chain moves 0→1→2→0, so its n-step point mass cycles with period three while its Cesàro average is uniform.

findings.diagram_content: Draw three nodes 0, 1, 2 in a directed cycle, label each edge probability 1, and place invariant vector π=(1/3,1/3,1/3) beside it. A small sequence beneath it may show δ_0, δ_1, δ_2 repeating and the three-term average π.
checks: Every node has exactly one outgoing and incoming edge, so each row and column sums to one.
Return times are 3,6,9,…, giving period 3 and T_x^+=3.
The n-step law cycles among point masses and stays at total-variation distance 2/3 from π; only Cesàro averages converge to π.
findings.status_note: Optional teaching support, not a defect; the exact cycle and numerical checks are already proved in the source.

findings.title: Leading-text loss concern rejected after coordinator recheck

frozen_source.claim: The definition begins “Let (A_i)_{i∈I} be a family of events in a probability space.”

rendered_evidence.visual_claim: At original resolution the visible line begins around the closing portion of the indexed-family expression; the opening “Let (A_i” is not legible in the captured tile. The frozen HTML contains the full source text and KaTeX MathML.

coordinator_recheck.result: Standalone original-resolution recheck visibly shows the full opening “Let (A_i)…” at the normal left inset. The initial apparent omission was a viewer observation error; there is no confirmed clipping defect.

findings.status_note: Rejected after independent coordinator recheck of the original tile. Preserve this record to prevent the false positive from being carried forward.
